summary: Broom Service is a bluffing-driven role-selection game where players choose bold or timid versions of witch and druid roles to deliver potions. The simultaneous reveal creates constant tension as bold actions are more powerful but can be blocked by other bold players.
praised: Clever push-your-luck role selection with real bluffing tension
Quick to teach and plays fast
Fun simultaneous-reveal moments that spark table talk
criticised: Can feel swingy or luck-driven in outcomes
Round structure can feel repetitive over 7 rounds

interaction.detail: Potions are delivered across one shared map, and players simultaneously choose roles knowing that multiple players being 'bold' on the same role causes a clash where only one succeeds and others can lose goods. This creates frequent indirect conflict over shared locations and a common potion supply, without any card or action that targets an opponent directly.

sources: potion delivery VP (per track space reached)
scoring.how_you_win: After 7 rounds of 4 turns each, whoever has earned the most VP from delivering potions to houses and building houses along the way wins.
